A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same adjoint-based PDE discovery work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including material renumbered or relocated in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original numerical PDE discovery experiments, including coefficient errors, recovered equations, execution times, and noise and temporal-sparsity tests in the main text and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds empirical analyses of incomplete candidate libraries, hyperparameter sensitivity, and denoising errors.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 add coefficient convergence at tolerance gamma_thr as an alternative trigger for thresholding, previously triggered only after Nthr epochs. The adjoint equations, objective, gradient averaging, and learning-rate formula remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate heat, Burgers’, Kuramoto–Sivashinsky, random-walk/Fokker–Planck, reaction-diffusion, and wave problems. The new analyses reuse retained tasks and vary candidate libraries or hyperparameters; the denoising illustration uses an already represented noise scenario.

E2.justification: PDE-FIND with STRidge remains the evaluated external comparator in the corresponding experiments. The comparisons between adjoint training with and without gradient averaging are also retained; no new comparison method is evaluated.

E3.justification: New Appendices C–D introduce controlled nine-versus-six-term Burgers’ libraries and hyperparameter sweeps on Nt = Nx = 100 grids. They track relative solution L2 error alongside coefficient error. These are added protocols; the original benchmark grids, preprocessing, and comparisons are retained.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands supplementary validation beyond the retained noise, temporal-sparsity, and thresholding tests. Appendix C tests omission of the true Burgers’ term, Appendix D systematically varies regularization, thresholding tolerance, and learning rate, and Figure 3 adds a denoising error analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report execution-time averages over ten independent runs and standard-deviation error bars in Section 3. The additions introduce no new seed information, repeated-run reporting practice, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Both tables and all pre-existing plots retain their results. Added findings concern controlled variants: the incomplete Burgers’ library yields f_t + (0.04f - 0.01f^3)_xx = 0 with relative L2 error O(10^-5), while Figures 18–19 add parameter-dependent error and convergence curves. Figure 3 adds denoising-error profiles.

T1.justification: New Appendix E adds a gradient-scaling argument and an O(h^(-dmax)) update-magnitude bound to justify the existing learning rate. Appendix C defines complete and incomplete candidate spaces. The original adjoint derivations are unchanged and move from Appendix C to Appendix F.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions and claims: adjoint-based discovery of PDE forms and coefficients, high accuracy, and favorable scaling relative to PDE-FIND on large datasets.

C2.justification: v3 adds qualifications about prior knowledge of PDE type, unstable intermediate equations, and solver suitability. Appendices C–D interpret residual stagnation as a possible incomplete-library diagnostic, qualify it under noise, and discuss accuracy, stability, and convergence tradeoffs. Section 7 expands the proposed mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: v3 specifies the new default gamma_thr = 10^-6 and documents hyperparameter ranges and fixed controls for the added studies. The finite-difference/Euler implementation and CPU disclosure are retained, with no change in code or data access information.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work survey are retained. Section 7 adds a claimed mechanistic distinction between multiplier-weighted errors in the adjoint approach and PDE-FIND’s pointwise loss, modestly extending the comparative positioning. The switch to author–year citations is only stylistic.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain largely intact. v3 adds localized explanations and appendix sections, relabels the former Appendix C as F, and changes citation style and reference ordering without extensively rewriting the retained text.

P2.justification: v3 adds the multipanel denoising illustration and Figures 17–19, changes title, author, heading, and header formatting, and relocates some figures through reflow. Existing plot designs and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendices C–D add useful evidence about failure with missing candidate terms and sensitivity to parameter choices, strengthening understanding of applicability while retaining the established results. These gains are partly offset by inconsistent thresholding guidance and Appendix E’s assertion of uniform convergence from an update-scaling bound alone.
